_comment: Copy to config.json and edit for your project. Every outlet below was live-verified 2026-08-26: real, currently-publishing newsletters, checked page by page for a public submission mechanism. Where one exists, submit_channel/submit_url_or_address name it for real (Console, Changelog News, the Cooperpress family, iOS Dev Weekly). Where none is discoverable, submit_channel is honestly 'unknown' with the homepage as the address - TLDR, TLDR AI, Hacker Newsletter, Ben's Bites, The Rundown AI, and Pointer all fall here; do not treat an 'unknown' entry as a green light to guess an address. alive_markers are short, verbatim, non-numeric phrases seen on each check_url at verification time (subscriber counts drift constantly and make poor markers). 'Dev Weekly' (devweekly.news) was investigated and found dormant since 2023, so it is excluded; iOS Dev Weekly is the real, currently-active outlet that search turned up in its place. Nothing here drafts a pitch or submits anything - scan only checks freshness, classifies, and records; a human drafts and submits behind the gate.

outlets.name: TLDR
outlets.format_note: No public submission mechanism found (checked the homepage, /newsletters, /blog, a live issue page, and the advertise subdomain). The only address on the site is a DMCA/copyright-notice contact, not a pitch channel - do not use it as one. Sponsorship runs separately through advertise.tldr.tech. Treat any pitch here as a cold approach.
outlets.audience_note: Daily tech-news roundup, 8,000,000+ readers, split into 14+ topic editions (tech, ai, dev, infosec, devops, and more).
alive_markers: summaries of the most interesting stories in startups

outlets.name: TLDR AI
outlets.format_note: Shares TLDR's general absence of a discoverable editorial intake path. Advertising only, via advertise.tldr.tech/sponsorship-opportunities.
outlets.audience_note: AI-focused daily edition for engineers, researchers, and technical professionals; ~1,100,000 subscribers.
alive_markers: covering AI news, research, and tools

outlets.name: Console
outlets.format_note: Email hello@console.dev with the tool's details. They look for developer tools with self-serve signup (no sales call needed to try it), workflow integration, active maintenance, and good docs; no sponsored reviews. Roughly 2-3 tools featured per week.
outlets.audience_note: Weekly devtools roundup for CTOs, engineering managers, and experienced developers; 30k+ subscribers, 77% with 5+ years coding experience.

outlets.name: Changelog News
outlets.format_note: Web form: URL, title, and a short note on why it's interesting (Markdown accepted). Self-submission is explicitly welcomed - 'submitting your own work is also encouraged.' Excludes how-tos/tutorials, commercial products (an open-source project reads as in scope; a paid product does not), and podcast-episode suggestions.
outlets.audience_note: Software newsletter and podcast, 26,000+ subscribers. Caveat as of this registry's build date: cadence has slowed sharply (issue #185 dated 2026-04-29 against a stated weekly rhythm) - confirm it is still actively publishing before investing time in a pitch.
alive_markers: if your fellow devs will find it interesting, submit it

outlets.name: Hacker Newsletter
outlets.format_note: No submission mechanism: content is curated from Hacker News itself rather than solicited directly, so the practical path is getting the link traction on HN. The only public intake found is a paid classified ad via an Airtable form linked from issue footers.
outlets.audience_note: Weekly hand-curated digest of the best Hacker News articles; 70,000+ subscribers.
alive_markers: hand-curated the best articles from Hacker News

outlets.name: Cooperpress (JavaScript Weekly / Node Weekly family)
outlets.format_note: One shared editorial address covers the whole family: JavaScript Weekly, Node Weekly, Frontend Focus, Ruby Weekly, Golang Weekly, React Status, Postgres Weekly (Python Weekly is a different publisher, not Cooperpress). No formal submission guidelines are published; the observed house format is a link plus a short blurb. Pick the one newsletter in the family that actually matches your project before pitching.
outlets.audience_note: JavaScript Weekly alone reaches 170,000+ developers; the family together spans JS, Node, frontend, Ruby, Go, React, and Postgres.
alive_markers: the ideal way to get a quick response is by emailing us

outlets.name: Ben's Bites
outlets.format_note: No editorial tip/submission channel is published (the old community link-sharing board is gone). The only verified addresses are partnership and support (shanice@bensbites.com, team@bensbites.co) - paid or support, not a pitch path.
outlets.audience_note: AI-focused newsletter on agents, tools, and builder news; 170,000+ subscribers. Note: .com is the canonical, currently-delivering domain - the older .co domain's newsletter delivery is dead, do not use it.
alive_markers: What I'm learning building with agents

outlets.name: The Rundown AI
outlets.format_note: No free submission path found; the only intake is a paid-advertising Typeform. support@therundown.ai is a general contact address, not a documented tips channel.
outlets.audience_note: AI news digest; 2,000,000+ readers across AI, Tech, and Robotics editions.
alive_markers: Get the latest AI news, understand why it matters

outlets.name: Pointer
outlets.format_note: No editorial submission mechanism found; the one published address (suraj@pointer.io) is for paid sponsorship. Curated reading-list format (outside writing, summarized) rather than a launch/tool-mention outlet.
outlets.audience_note: Twice-weekly engineering-leadership reading list (leadership, management, career growth) - a narrow fit unless your project is about engineering management, not general dev tooling. ~60,000 subscribers. Caveat: the site returns HTTP 403 to non-browser fetches, so this module's freshness check will likely report it unreachable even when the site is fine - verify by hand in a real browser before trusting that status.

outlets.name: iOS Dev Weekly
outlets.format_note: Structured form: name, email, link, link origin, whether it's a blog post or a Swift library, and a short rationale. Swift/Apple-platform projects only - skip this one for anything else.
outlets.audience_note: Weekly hand-curated links for Swift and Apple-platform developers, published since 2011 by Dave Verwer.
alive_markers: Why should this link be included in iOS Dev Weekly?
